articles.title: US CPI preview: 14 investment bank forecasters see energy lifting headline to 3.6%, core held near 0.2%
articles.expand: The headline jump is largely priced in, so the market reaction will hinge on core. A print at the top of the forecast range, around 0.24% or higher, would back the Fed officials warning that inflation is broadening and firm December hike pricing, lifting front-end yields and the dollar. A reading at the soft end, near 0.16% to 0.18%, would support New York Fed President Williams’ view that price pressures are shock-driven and could trim expectations for tightening beyond this year. articles.title: ICYMI - Three Fed officials signal inflation fight continues; Williams sees no 2027 hike

That should limit the upside for longer-dated Treasury yields and the dollar unless the data turns. Barkin’s warning that shocks are continuing gives the hawkish camp an opening if inflation stays sticky. Oil is the swing factor. Williams’ benign outlook assumes energy won’t add to inflation next year, so a renewed crude surge, for example from escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites, would undercut that view ...

articles.title: Fed’s Collins says uncertainty is elevated as she watches breadth of inflation pressures
articles.expand: Collins’ focus on how widespread inflation is moves attention to core and services prices, not just the headline energy-driven numbers. Signs of fuel costs spreading into broader prices would firm December hike pricing and support front-end yields and the dollar. For oil, that means sustained strength in crude and products now carries a second-round risk the Fed is explicitly watching. The higher oil price assumptions, at $96 a barrel this year and $87 next, effectively validate a prolonged risk premium in crude. articles.expand: The minutes read hawkish, not unexpectedly, with the board explicitly keeping further hikes on the table and markets already pricing roughly another 15 basis points by year-end and 30 basis points in the first half of 2027. Oil is central to the outlook: domestic fuel prices were running well above the RBA’s August assumptions, and any further escalation of the Iran war would feed directly into the risk of more tightening. articles.title: Japan wholesale inflation misses at 6.8% but stays high enough to keep BOJ hike alive
articles.expand: The miss trims some urgency from the hike narrative, but an annual pace near 7% and surging import costs leave the case for tightening intact, keeping Japanese yields and BOJ pricing sensitive to any hawkish signals. The weak yen is the key amplifier: with oil prices elevated by the Iran war, every leg lower in the currency raises the yen cost of energy and feeds back into pipeline inflation. A rate hike that narrows the gap with other central banks could support the yen and ease that pressure, which is part of the case for acting sooner.
